brief: 6 writing tips for founders who hate writing. Editorial voice, gentle but pointed.

slots.headline: Six Ways to Write Better Without Learning to Love It

slots.title: Talk It Out
slots.body: Record yourself explaining the idea to a patient friend, then transcribe the best sentences. Your voice already has the rhythm; you simply need to capture it on the page. Editing is far easier than facing a blank screen.

slots.title: One Messy Sentence
slots.body: Start with an ugly first sentence that you would never show anyone. The goal is momentum, not perfection. You can polish a rough paragraph, but you cannot sculpt a blank document.

slots.title: Kill Your Adverbs
slots.body: Strip away words that try too hard to persuade. Very, really, and incredibly are crutches that weaken your stance. Let your argument stand clean and unadorned; confidence speaks quietly.

slots.title: Write the Reply
slots.body: Imagine a skeptical reader asking why this matters. Answer them directly, without jargon or performance. Writing becomes easier when you stop addressing a crowd and start talking to one person.

slots.title: Read It Aloud
slots.body: If a sentence catches in your throat, it will trip your reader too. Trust your ear over every grammar rule. Clarity sounds like a conversation, not a press release.

slots.title: Know When to Stop
slots.body: Perfectionism is often a disguise for fear. Ship the piece when it is clear and honest, not when it is flawless. Your reader wants your thinking, not your anxiety.
